guide.title: Greenwich, London: Cutty Sark, the Old Royal Naval College and the prime meridian
guide.intro: Greenwich is a riverside town in south-east London that gives its name to a royal borough running east to Woolwich and south to Eltham. Its core sits inside the Maritime Greenwich World Heritage Site, NHLE 1000096, whose core area covers 109.51 hectares: Cutty Sark in a dry berth, the four quarters of the Old Royal Naval College, the National Maritime Museum and the Queen's House on the axis behind them, a covered market trading since 1737 and a domed entrance to the foot tunnel under the Thames. Greenwich Park rises from the town to the Royal Observatory and the prime meridian, with Ranger's House on the Blackheath side. East and south the borough turns to Jacobean Charlton House, the Royal Arsenal at Woolwich, a 1930s house grafted onto the medieval palace at Eltham and a folly tower on Shooters Hill.

sections.heading: Maritime Greenwich, the town centre and the Peninsula
sections.body:
The riverside core of Greenwich sits inside the Maritime Greenwich World Heritage Site, NHLE 1000096, whose core area covers 109.51 hectares and whose buffer zone covers 174.91 hectares. Cutty Sark stands in a dry berth at King William Walk, Grade I listed as NHLE 1079013, with the hull raised so that visitors walk beneath it; she opens daily 10am to 5pm except on 24, 25 and 26 December, and adult admission is £22. The Old Royal Naval College fills four separately listed quarters, all Grade I from 8 June 1973 — King William's, NHLE 1211426, which holds the Painted Hall, Queen Mary's, NHLE 1211384, which holds the Chapel, King Charles, NHLE 1211337, and Queen Anne's, NHLE 1290044. Its grounds open 8am to 11pm and are free; the Painted Hall opens 10am to 5pm at £19 for adults, and talks about it run every half hour from 11am to 4pm. The Queen's House stands on the axis between the college and Greenwich Park, joined to the National Maritime Museum's wings by colonnades. Both are free and open 10am to 5pm, and Yinka Shonibare's Nelson's Ship in a Bottle stands outside the museum on its south side.

Greenwich Market trades every day from 10am to 5.30pm on College Approach, established in 1737 by the market's own account and now, spread across two sites, over 120 shops and stalls. Its entrance arch is Grade II listed, NHLE 1358951, and the terraces around it carry their own entries at 9-21 College Approach, NHLE 1358952, 2-5 College Approach, NHLE 1079030, and 8A and 8B College Approach, NHLE 1079033. On Greenwich Church Street the parish church of St Alfege, Grade I listed as NHLE 1358970, opens Tuesday to Sunday 11am to 4pm, with free recitals at 1.05pm on Thursdays and Saturdays. In Cutty Sark Gardens the domed entrance building to the Greenwich Foot Tunnel, Grade II listed as NHLE 1289371, opens onto a free pedestrian route under the Thames to Island Gardens in Tower Hamlets; the Royal Borough of Greenwich publishes the tunnel and lift status and states that cycling through the tunnel is not permitted.

Greenwich Peninsula is the loop of the Thames north of the town, rebuilt around The O2 on Peninsula Square: an arena with a cinema, restaurants and bars under a tented roof, open daily 10am to 10pm, with the venues inside keeping their own hours. North Greenwich, the Jubilee line station serving it, is 295 m from the arena by TfL's measure, and North Greenwich Pier, on river-bus routes RB1 and RB6, is 412 m.

sections.heading: Greenwich Park and Blackheath
sections.body:
Greenwich Park is a Royal Park registered at Grade I on 1 October 1987, NHLE 1000174, with a registered area of 74.51 hectares that lies wholly within the core area of the Maritime Greenwich World Heritage Site, NHLE 1000096. Pedestrian gates open 6am to 8pm and vehicle gates 7am to 8pm, and Blackheath Gate, St Mary's Gate and Park Row Gate are among them. Two scheduled monuments lie inside the park, a Romano-Celtic temple, NHLE 1021439, and an Anglo-Saxon cemetery, NHLE 1021440; scheduled monuments carry no grade. The boundary wall around the park is Grade II listed, NHLE 1290730, and the Standard Reservoir conduit house within it is Grade II*, NHLE 1393455.

On Blackheath Avenue inside the park stands the Royal Observatory, whose buildings carry six list entries: Flamsteed House, the former Great Equatorial Building, the Transit House and the wall and clock to the right of the entrance gates at Grade I, NHLE 1358976, 1078998, 1220877 and 1220888, and the South Building and the Altazimuth Pavilion at Grade II, NHLE 1244325 and 1031860. The observatory is also a scheduled monument covering 0.53 hectares, NHLE 1002036, its entry amended on 9 October 2024. It opens daily except on 24, 25 and 26 December, 10am to 5pm for most of the year with last entry at 4.15pm, and 10am to 6pm in September with last entry at 5pm; adult admission is £24. The Grade II statue of General Wolfe, NHLE 1358977, stands immediately east of it.

Blackheath is divided between two boroughs and the boundary runs across the heath. Ranger's House, Grade I listed as NHLE 1218679, stands on Chesterfield Walk against the western edge of Greenwich Park facing the heath and holds the Wernher Collection; English Heritage opens it on select dates only and takes bookings online or on 020 8853 0035. Blackheath village and Blackheath Rail Station are in the London Borough of Lewisham. TfL measures 474 m from the heath at 51.4700, 0.0100 to Blackheath station, and 1,054 m from Ranger's House, against 1,079 m to Greenwich and 1,105 m to Maze Hill.

sections.heading: Woolwich, Charlton and Eltham
sections.body:
East and south of the park the borough carries listed buildings rather than institutions. Charlton House stands on Charlton Road at SE7 7TH, Grade I listed as NHLE 1218593, with three further Grade I entries on the same site: the garden house to the north-west, now a public lavatory, NHLE 1291892, the gateway on the axis west of the house, NHLE 1358935, and the stable buildings to the south-west, NHLE 1079066. It is in use as a community and library building with a cafe. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.

At Woolwich the Royal Arsenal carries the Royal Brass Foundry, Grade I listed as NHLE 1078956, with the Grand Store ranges, NHLE 1078958, the Board Room, NHLE 1359015, and the Dial Square entrance range, NHLE 1211005, at Grade II*. The foundry is not routinely open to visitors and is seen from outside. Woolwich Town Hall on Wellington Street is Grade II* listed, NHLE 1289668, a working council building whose Victoria Hall opens to the public only occasionally, and the Granada Cinema on Powis Street is Grade II*, NHLE 1212651. On Woolwich Common the Rotunda, the former Royal Artillery Museum building, is Grade II*, NHLE 1078987, as are the Royal Artillery Barracks main building, NHLE 1078918, and the Royal Military Academy main building, NHLE 1358936.

At Eltham the medieval Great Hall of Eltham Palace, Grade I listed as NHLE 1079041, carries the Grade II* house of the 1930s built onto it, NHLE 1212906, in gardens registered at Grade II* on 2 December 1998, NHLE 1001410, covering 8.27 hectares, over a scheduled monument of 5.40 hectares, NHLE 1014833. The moat crossings are Grade I: the north bridge, NHLE 1218925, and the remains of the south bridge, NHLE 1358958. English Heritage publishes no standard hours for the palace and directs visitors to 020 8294 2548 or 0370 333 1181. On Shooters Hill, Severndroog Castle in Castle Wood is Grade II* listed as NHLE 1289792, with a start date of 1784 recorded in OpenStreetMap; its tea room opens Thursday to Sunday 9am to 3.30pm and its viewing platform and galleries on Sundays 10am to 3pm, with last entry at 2.45pm.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
Greenwich is served by the DLR, the Jubilee line, the Elizabeth line, Southeastern and Thameslink national rail, Uber Boat river-bus routes RB1 and RB6, the Woolwich Ferry and the London Cable Car. There is no tube other than the Jubilee line at North Greenwich.

For the town centre, take the DLR to Cutty Sark (for Maritime Greenwich), which TfL puts 146 m from Greenwich Market, or a Southeastern or Thameslink train to Greenwich, 438 m, whose DLR platforms are 458 m. Greenwich Pier, on RB1 and RB6, is 295 m. Maze Hill is 845 m from the market and 682 m from the Royal Observatory, and Cutty Sark DLR is 856 m from the observatory, uphill through the park. From the north bank, walk through the Greenwich Foot Tunnel from Island Gardens DLR station, which TfL puts 652 m from the tunnel's south entrance building and 758 m from Cutty Sark DLR station.

For the Peninsula, take the Jubilee line to North Greenwich, 295 m from The O2, or the London Cable Car, which shares the same interchange, naptanId HUBNGW. North Greenwich Pier is 412 m away on RB1 and RB6. TfL also returns bus routes 108, 129, 132, 161, 180, 188, 335, 422, 486, N472 and SL11 at North Greenwich.

For Woolwich, take the Elizabeth line to Woolwich, or the DLR, Southeastern or Thameslink to Woolwich Arsenal; TfL gives 265 m between the two stations. Woolwich Town Hall is 374 m from Woolwich Arsenal, 577 m from Woolwich Elizabeth line station and 690 m from Woolwich Dockyard. Woolwich Arsenal Pier is 585 m on RB1 and RB6 and the Woolwich Ferry south pier 749 m. For Charlton House, take Southeastern or Thameslink to Charlton, 856 m away. For Eltham Palace, Mottingham is 768 m on Southeastern and Eltham 1,011 m on Southeastern and Thameslink; Eltham is also the nearest station to Severndroog Castle at 1,265 m, with Falconwood 1,540 m. Blackheath Rail Station, 474 m from the heath, is in the London Borough of Lewisham.

faq.question: What is inside the Maritime Greenwich World Heritage Site?
faq.answer: The core area of the Maritime Greenwich World Heritage Site, NHLE 1000096, covers 109.51 hectares, with a buffer zone of 174.91 hectares. Cutty Sark, the National Maritime Museum and Ranger's House sit inside the core area, and Greenwich Park's 74.51 registered hectares lie wholly within it. The Old Royal Naval College, the Queen's House, the covered market and the foot tunnel's domed entrance stand in the same riverside core. World Heritage Sites carry no grade.

faq.question: What does it cost to visit Cutty Sark, the Royal Observatory and the Painted Hall?
faq.answer: Cutty Sark is £22 for an adult, £11 for a child aged 4 to 15 and £16.50 for a student, with under-4s free. The Royal Observatory is £24 for an adult, £12 for a child aged 4 to 15 and £18 for a student, with under-4s free. General admission to the Painted Hall at the Old Royal Naval College is £19 for adults and free for children age 16 and under, up to four children with a paying adult. The National Maritime Museum, the Queen's House, Greenwich Park, Greenwich Market and St Alfege are free.

faq.question: Where does the Greenwich Foot Tunnel come out?
faq.answer: The tunnel runs under the Thames from Cutty Sark Gardens to Island Gardens in Tower Hamlets. The domed south entrance building is Grade II listed, NHLE 1289371, and the north entrance at Island Gardens is separately Grade II listed, NHLE 1065141. TfL puts Island Gardens DLR station 652 m from the south entrance building. The Royal Borough of Greenwich publishes the tunnel and lift status and states that cycling through the tunnel is not permitted. No source states opening hours for it, so none are given here.

faq.question: Which station serves The O2?
faq.answer: North Greenwich, which the venue names as its station and describes as a London Underground station served by the Jubilee line. TfL lists it as a combined tube and cable-car interchange, naptanId HUBNGW, 295 m from the arena, with North Greenwich Pier 412 m away on river-bus routes RB1 and RB6. The operator gives the journey as 20 minutes from Central London and 10 minutes from Stratford, and publishes separate arrival routes for tube and train, Uber Boat by Thames Clippers, bus and the IFS Cloud Cable Car.

faq.question: Are Eltham Palace and Ranger's House open to visitors?
faq.answer: Both are ticketed and managed by English Heritage, and neither publishes standard opening hours, so none are given here. English Heritage states that Ranger's House, Grade I listed as NHLE 1218679, is open on select dates and takes bookings online or on 020 8853 0035. For Eltham Palace, whose Great Hall is Grade I listed as NHLE 1079041, it directs visitors to 020 8294 2548 or 0370 333 1181.

faq.question: Is Blackheath in Greenwich?
faq.answer: The heath is divided, and the boundary runs across it. Ranger's House on Chesterfield Walk, Grade I listed as NHLE 1218679, is on the Greenwich side, standing against the western edge of Greenwich Park and holding the Wernher Collection. Blackheath village and Blackheath Rail Station are in the London Borough of Lewisham. TfL measures 474 m from the heath at 51.4700, 0.0100 to the station and 1,054 m from Ranger's House.

photos.title: Cutty Sark in her dry berth at King William Walk, Greenwich
photos.description: The clipper seen from off her port bow against a pale evening sky, black hull and gilded lettering above the glazed canopy that roofs the dry berth. The bowsprit reaches out to the right and all three masts stand fully rigged, with the trees of Cutty Sark Gardens at the left edge.
photos.author: Ryan Hodnett

places.name: Cutty Sark
places.address: King William Walk, Greenwich, London SE10 9HT
places.summary: Cutty Sark is a tea clipper in a dry berth at King William Walk, operated by Royal Museums Greenwich, with the hull raised so that visitors walk beneath it. She opens daily 10am to 5pm, last entry 4.15pm, except on 24, 25 and 26 December. Admission is £22 for an adult, £11 for a child aged 4 to 15 and £16.50 for a student, and under-4s are free. The operator invites visitors to explore the main deck, walk beneath the ship and see how the crew lived.
places.history: The ship is Grade I listed, NHLE 1079013, first listed on 8 June 1973, at national grid reference TQ 38305 77866. OpenStreetMap records a start date of 1869 for the hull and tags her historic=ship. She sits inside the core area of the Maritime Greenwich World Heritage Site, NHLE 1000096, which covers 109.51 hectares against a buffer zone of 174.91 hectares.

places.name: Old Royal Naval College
places.address: Old Royal Naval College, Greenwich, London SE10 9NN
places.summary: The Old Royal Naval College is a group of four quarters on the Greenwich riverside, addressed by the operator at SE10 9NN. The Painted Hall, the Chapel and the visitor centre open daily 10am to 5pm, and the grounds daily 8am to 11pm. The grounds are free; general admission to the Painted Hall is £19 for adults and free for children age 16 and under, up to four children with a paying adult. Talks about the Painted Hall take place every half hour from 11am to 4pm. The operator gives Greenwich station as an 11-minute walk and Maze Hill as 15 minutes, both served by Southeastern and Thameslink.
places.history: The four quarters are separately Grade I listed, all first listed on 8 June 1973: King William's, NHLE 1211426, which contains the Painted Hall; Queen Mary's, NHLE 1211384, which contains the Chapel; King Charles, NHLE 1211337; and Queen Anne's, NHLE 1290044. The west entrance gates, piers and lodges are Grade I, NHLE 1078973, and the east gate lodges NHLE 1358993. The site overlies the remains of Greenwich Palace, a scheduled monument of 10.22 hectares, NHLE 1410710, scheduled on 22 March 2013; a second scheduled monument, Greenwich Hospital (RN College), NHLE 1002037, is a legacy point entry covering 0.0025 hectares at TQ 38503 77929. Wikidata gives an inception date of 1696 and places the college in the Royal Borough of Greenwich. Sir James Thornhill designed the Painted Hall's scheme and painted it between 1707 and 1726; the operator states that it features more than 3,700 square metres of Baroque walls and ceilings with 200 figures including kings, queens and mythological creatures.

places.name: National Maritime Museum
places.summary: The National Maritime Museum stands on Romney Road at SE10 9NF and opens daily 10am to 5pm, last entry 4.15pm, except on 24, 25 and 26 December. Entry is free and the operator recommends booking. Yinka Shonibare's Nelson's Ship in a Bottle stands outside the museum on its south side, having earlier been a temporary Fourth Plinth commission in Trafalgar Square.
places.history: The museum building is Grade I listed, NHLE 1211481, first listed on 8 June 1973, at national grid reference TQ 38711 77697. The forecourt railings and gates are Grade II, NHLE 1211484, and the east wall, railings and gates NHLE 1290310. The museum sits inside the 109.51-hectare core area of the Maritime Greenwich World Heritage Site, NHLE 1000096.

places.name: Queen's House
places.summary: The Queen's House stands on the axis between the Old Royal Naval College and Greenwich Park, joined to the museum wings by colonnades. It opens daily 10am to 5pm except on 24, 25 and 26 December, and the operator states that the Queen's House is free to visit.
places.history: Wikidata gives an inception date of 1616. The building is a scheduled monument, NHLE 1002060, entered on the National Heritage List under the name Queen's House and covering 0.15 hectares at TQ 38714 77691; scheduled monuments carry no grade. Its Grade I listing is entered under the name National Maritime Museum, NHLE 1211481, the same number Wikidata Q564981 carries for the house.

places.name: Greenwich Market
places.summary: Greenwich Market trades daily from 10am to 5.30pm on College Approach at SE10 9HY and is free to enter. The market's own site says it was established in 1737 and that, spread across two sites, it has over 120 shops and stalls to discover. OpenStreetMap records the same trading hours and the same start date of 1737.
places.history: The market entrance arch is Grade II listed, NHLE 1358951, listed on 8 June 1973 and named simply MARKET ENTRANCE on the National Heritage List, at TQ 38326 77758. The terraces around it carry their own Grade II entries: 9-21 College Approach, NHLE 1358952, 2-5 College Approach, NHLE 1079030, and 8A and 8B College Approach, NHLE 1079033. The Admiral Hardy public house on the market's edge is Grade II, NHLE 1079032, and the Coach and Horses NHLE 1214365.

places.name: Church of St Alfege
places.address: Greenwich Church Street, Greenwich, London SE10 9BJ
places.summary: St Alfege is a working parish church on Greenwich Church Street at SE10 9BJ, free to enter and open Tuesday to Sunday 11am to 4pm. It closes on Mondays except bank holidays, when it opens 11am to 4pm. Free lunchtime recitals run at 1.05pm on Thursdays and Saturdays. The parish records the dedication to St Alfege, the Archbishop of Canterbury who was martyred on this site in 1012.
places.history: The church is Grade I listed, NHLE 1358970, first listed on 19 October 1951, at national grid reference TQ 38306 77605. The parish states that it was the first London church designed by Nicholas Hawksmoor, and names Thomas Tallis, General James Wolfe and John Flamsteed among the figures connected with it.

places.name: Greenwich Foot Tunnel
places.address: Cutty Sark Gardens, Greenwich Church Street, Greenwich, London SE10 9HT
places.summary: The Greenwich Foot Tunnel is a free pedestrian route under the Thames, entered on the south bank through the domed building in Cutty Sark Gardens beside Cutty Sark. The council describes it as connecting Cutty Sark on the south bank of the River Thames to Island Gardens, Tower Hamlets, and states that cycling through the tunnel is not permitted. The Royal Borough of Greenwich publishes the tunnel and lift status at royalgreenwich.gov.uk and says that from July to December it will be working to replace lift parts and upgrade the fire alarm system. No source states opening hours for the tunnel, so none are given here.
places.history: The south entrance building is Grade II listed, NHLE 1289371, listed on 26 June 1975, at national grid reference TQ 38263 77914; Historic England names the entry ENTRANCE BUILDING TO GREENWICH FOOTWAY TUNNEL. The north entrance at Island Gardens is separately Grade II listed, NHLE 1065141. TfL measures 652 m from the south entrance building at 51.4828, -0.0096 to Island Gardens DLR station, and 758 m from Cutty Sark DLR station.

places.name: Royal Observatory Greenwich
places.summary: The Royal Observatory stands on Blackheath Avenue inside Greenwich Park at SE10 8XJ and is operated by Royal Museums Greenwich. It opens daily except on 24, 25 and 26 December: 10am to 6pm in September, with last entry at 5pm, and 10am to 5pm for the rest of the year, with last entry at 4.15pm. Admission is £24 for an adult, £12 for a child aged 4 to 15 and £18 for a student, and under-4s are free.
places.history: The observatory's buildings carry six list entries. Flamsteed House is Grade I, NHLE 1358976, first listed on 8 June 1973 at TQ 38847 77335; the former Great Equatorial Building is Grade I, NHLE 1078998; the Transit House Grade I, NHLE 1220877; the wall and clock to the right of the entrance gates Grade I, NHLE 1220888; the South Building Grade II, NHLE 1244325; and the Altazimuth Pavilion Grade II, NHLE 1031860, added on 21 August 2002. The observatory is also a scheduled monument covering 0.53 hectares, NHLE 1002036, its entry amended on 9 October 2024; scheduled monuments carry no grade. The Grade II statue of General Wolfe, NHLE 1358977, listed on 8 June 1973, stands immediately east of the observatory.

places.name: Greenwich Park
places.address: Greenwich Park, Foyle Road, London SE3 7RH
places.summary: Greenwich Park is a Royal Park of 74.51 registered hectares, NHLE 1000174, free to enter, with pedestrian gates open 6am to 8pm and vehicle gates 7am to 8pm. Blackheath Gate, St Mary's Gate and Park Row Gate are among its entrances, and the Royal Observatory stands within it on Blackheath Avenue.
places.history: The park was registered at Grade I on the Register of Parks and Gardens on 1 October 1987, NHLE 1000174, with a registered area of 74.51 hectares. Two scheduled monuments lie within it: a Romano-Celtic temple, NHLE 1021439, and an Anglo-Saxon cemetery, NHLE 1021440; scheduled monuments carry no grade. The registered polygon lies wholly within the core area of the Maritime Greenwich World Heritage Site, NHLE 1000096, whose core covers 109.51 hectares and whose buffer zone covers 174.91 hectares. The boundary wall around the park is Grade II listed, NHLE 1290730, and the Standard Reservoir conduit house within it Grade II*, NHLE 1393455.

places.name: Ranger's House and the Wernher Collection
places.summary: Ranger's House holds the Wernher Collection on Chesterfield Walk at SE10 8QX and is managed by English Heritage, which states that Ranger's House is open on select dates and directs visitors to book online or telephone 020 8853 0035. No source states standard opening hours, so none are given here. The house stands against the western edge of Greenwich Park, facing Blackheath. TfL measures 1,054 m from it to Blackheath station, 1,079 m to Greenwich and 1,105 m to Maze Hill.
places.history: The house is Grade I listed, NHLE 1218679, first listed on 19 October 1951, at national grid reference TQ 38887 76832. That grid reference falls inside the core area of the Maritime Greenwich World Heritage Site, NHLE 1000096, and outside the registered boundary of Greenwich Park, NHLE 1000174. A commemorative plaque on the house records that Philip, 4th Earl of Chesterfield lived there.

places.name: The O2
places.address: Peninsula Square, Greenwich Peninsula, London SE10 0DX
places.summary: The O2 stands on Peninsula Square at SE10 0DX and is open daily from 10am to 10pm, with the venues, restaurants, bars and leisure activities inside keeping their own hours. The operator names North Greenwich as its station, a London Underground station served by the Jubilee line, and publishes separate arrival routes for tube and train, Uber Boat by Thames Clippers, bus and the IFS Cloud Cable Car.
places.history: The operator gives the journey as 20 minutes from Central London and 10 minutes from Stratford. TfL lists North Greenwich as a combined tube and cable-car interchange, naptanId HUBNGW, 295 m from the arena, with North Greenwich Pier 412 m away on river-bus routes RB1 and RB6. The station's own postal address is 5 Millenium Way, London SE10 0PH.

places.name: Charlton House
places.summary: Charlton House is a Jacobean house on Charlton Road at SE7 7TH, in use as a community and library building with a cafe. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here. Charlton rail station is 856 m away, served by Southeastern and Thameslink.
places.history: The house is Grade I listed, NHLE 1218593, first listed on 19 October 1951, at national grid reference TQ4155577714. Three further Grade I entries cover the same site: the garden house to the north-west, now a public lavatory, NHLE 1291892; the gateway on the axis west of the house, NHLE 1358935; and the stable buildings to the south-west, NHLE 1079066. Nominatim places the house in the Royal Borough of Greenwich at 51.4807, 0.0371.

places.name: Eltham Palace and Gardens
places.summary: Eltham Palace and Gardens is a medieval royal palace with a house of the 1930s built onto it, at Court Yard in Eltham, SE9 5QE. It is ticketed and managed by English Heritage. No source states standard opening hours, so none are given here; English Heritage directs visitors to 020 8294 2548 or 0370 333 1181. Mottingham rail station is 768 m away on Southeastern, and Eltham 1,011 m away on Southeastern and Thameslink.
places.history: The medieval Great Hall is Grade I listed, NHLE 1079041, first listed on 8 June 1973, at TQ 42411 73987. Eltham Court, the house of the 1930s, is Grade II* listed, NHLE 1212906, listed on 6 July 1981. The gardens were registered at Grade II* on 2 December 1998, NHLE 1001410, covering 8.27 hectares, and the palace is a scheduled monument of 5.40 hectares, NHLE 1014833, scheduled on 9 October 1981 and amended on 10 June 1998; scheduled monuments carry no grade. The moat crossings are Grade I: the north bridge, NHLE 1218925, and the remains of the south bridge, NHLE 1358958. The inner courtyard walls with adjoining chambers are Grade I, NHLE 1218900.

places.name: Severndroog Castle
places.address: Castle Wood, Shooters Hill, London SE18 3RT
places.summary: Severndroog Castle is a tower in Castle Wood on Shooters Hill at SE18 3RT. The operator publishes separate hours for the tea room, Thursday to Sunday 9am to 3.30pm, and for the viewing platform and galleries, Sunday only 10am to 3pm with last entry at 2.45pm. Eltham rail station is 1,265 m away on Southeastern and Thameslink, and Falconwood 1,540 m away on Southeastern.
places.history: The tower is Grade II* listed, NHLE 1289792, listed on 26 March 1954, at national grid reference TQ 43190 76196; Historic England names the entry SEVERNDROOG CASTLE, CASTLE WOOD PARK. OpenStreetMap records a start date of 1784 for the tower.

places.name: Royal Arsenal Brass Foundry
places.summary: The Royal Brass Foundry stands on the Royal Arsenal site in Woolwich, SE18 6GH. It is not routinely open to visitors and is seen from outside. Woolwich Arsenal station, on the DLR, Southeastern and Thameslink, and Woolwich Elizabeth line station are 265 m apart by TfL's measure.
places.history: The foundry is Grade I listed, NHLE 1078956, first listed on 8 June 1973, at national grid reference TQ 43737 79063; Historic England names the entry ROYAL ARSENAL BRASS FOUNDRY ROYAL FOUNDRY. On the same site the Grand Store ranges, NHLE 1078958, the Board Room, NHLE 1359015, and the Dial Square entrance range, NHLE 1211005, are Grade II*. On Woolwich Common the Rotunda, the former Royal Artillery Museum building, is Grade II*, NHLE 1078987, as are the Royal Artillery Barracks main building, NHLE 1078918, and the Royal Military Academy main building, NHLE 1358936.

places.name: Woolwich Town Hall
places.summary: Woolwich Town Hall is a working council building on Wellington Street at SE18 6PE, and public access to the Victoria Hall inside is occasional. Measured from the building at 51.4899, 0.0646, TfL puts Woolwich Arsenal station 374 m away, Woolwich Elizabeth line station 577 m and Woolwich Dockyard 690 m.
places.history: The town hall is Grade II* listed, NHLE 1289668, first listed on 8 June 1973, at national grid reference TQ4345278739. OpenStreetMap tags it amenity=townhall and historic=townhall and links Wikidata Q17551089. The Granada Cinema on Powis Street is also Grade II*, NHLE 1212651.

links.note: Blackheath is divided: Ranger's House on Chesterfield Walk is in Greenwich, while Blackheath village and Blackheath Rail Station are in Lewisham.
The Greenwich Foot Tunnel runs under the Thames to Island Gardens in Tower Hamlets, 652 m from its south entrance building by TfL's measure.
The Thames Path runs from Greenwich through Rotherhithe to Bankside, and Brunel's Thames Tunnel crossed the river sixty years before the foot tunnel.

entries.name: Cutty Sark

entries.name: Old Royal Naval College

entries.name: Queen's House
entries.note: Free to visit, 10am to 5pm, on the axis between the college and the park; a scheduled monument of 0.15 hectares, NHLE 1002060, dated to 1616 by Wikidata.

entries.name: Greenwich Market
entries.note: Over 120 shops and stalls on College Approach across two sites, trading daily 10am to 5.30pm; the market's own site dates it to 1737.

entries.name: Church of St Alfege
entries.note: A working parish church, Grade I listed as NHLE 1358970, open Tuesday to Sunday 11am to 4pm, with free recitals at 1.05pm on Thursdays and Saturdays.

entries.name: Greenwich Foot Tunnel
entries.note: A free pedestrian route under the Thames from Cutty Sark Gardens to Island Gardens in Tower Hamlets; TfL measures 652 m from the south entrance building.

entries.name: Royal Observatory Greenwich
entries.note: The prime meridian on Blackheath Avenue, with Flamsteed House Grade I as NHLE 1358976; £24 for an adult, 10am to 5pm and to 6pm in September.

entries.name: Greenwich Park
entries.note: A Royal Park of 74.51 registered hectares, NHLE 1000174, pedestrian gates 6am to 8pm; Blackheath Gate, St Mary's Gate and Park Row Gate are among them.

entries.name: Ranger's House and the Wernher Collection
entries.note: A Grade I house on Chesterfield Walk, NHLE 1218679; English Heritage opens it on select dates only and takes bookings online or on 020 8853 0035.

entries.name: The O2
entries.note: Open daily 10am to 10pm on Peninsula Square, with the venues inside keeping their own hours; North Greenwich on the Jubilee line is 295 m away.

entries.name: Charlton House
entries.note: A Jacobean house on Charlton Road, Grade I listed as NHLE 1218593, now a community and library building with a cafe; no source states its hours.

entries.name: Eltham Palace and Gardens
entries.note: A medieval Great Hall, Grade I listed as NHLE 1079041, with a Grade II* house of the 1930s built onto it, NHLE 1212906, in 8.27 hectares of gardens.

entries.name: Severndroog Castle
entries.note: A tower of 1784 in Castle Wood, Grade II* listed as NHLE 1289792; tea room Thursday to Sunday 9am to 3.30pm, viewing platform Sundays 10am to 3pm.

entries.name: Royal Arsenal Brass Foundry
entries.note: The Royal Brass Foundry on the Royal Arsenal site, Grade I listed as NHLE 1078956; it is not routinely open to visitors and is seen from outside.

entries.name: Woolwich Town Hall
entries.note: A working council building on Wellington Street, Grade II* listed as NHLE 1289668, 374 m from Woolwich Arsenal station by TfL's measure.
